import json
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from .world import World, DIRECTIONS, Room, Item, WorldError
from .parser import Command, ParseError

# --- Custom Errors ---
class SaveError(ValueError):
    """Raised when game save/load operations fail."""
    pass

# --- Game Class ---
class Game:
    """Represents a player's session state in the adventure world."""
    def __init__(self, world: World):
        self.world = world
        self.room_id: str = world.start
        # Items start empty, but we populate with items from the start room
        initial_items = world.rooms[world.start].items
        self.inventory: List[str] = list(initial_items)
        self.moves: int = 0

    def items_in(self, room_id: str) -> List[str]:
        """Returns a new list of item IDs currently in the specified room, in order."""
        return list(self.world.rooms[room_id].items)

    def do(self, line: str) -> str:
        """Runs one command and returns the response text."""
        # 1. Handle 'look' commands
        if line.startswith('look'):
            args = line[4:].strip().split() if len(line) > 4 else []
            arg_name = args[0] if args else None

            if not arg_name:
                # look command
                room = self.world.rooms[self.room_id]
                name_lines = [room.name, room.description]
                
                # Exits
                exit_dirs = [d for d, r_id in room.exits.items() if r_id in self.world.rooms]
                if exit_dirs:
                    exit_line = f"Exits: {', '.join(exit_dirs)}."
                else:
                    exit_line = "Exits: none."
                
                # Items
                room_item_ids = room.items
                if room_item_ids:
                    item_names = [self.world.items[i_id].name for i_id in room_item_ids]
                    item_line = f"You see: {', '.join(item_names)}."
                else:
                    item_line = ""
                
                return "\n".join(name_lines + [exit_line] + ([item_line] if item_line else []))
            else:
                # look X command
                # Search in room first
                room_item_ids = room.items
                match = next((i_id for i_id in room_item_ids if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
                
                if match:
                    item = self.world.items[match]
                    return f"{item.description}"
                
                # Search in inventory
                match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
                
                if match:
                    item = self.world.items[match]
                    return f"{item.description}"
                else:
                    return "You see no {arg_name} here."
        
        # 2. Handle 'go DIR' command
        elif line.startswith('go '):
            direction = line[3:].strip()
            if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
                return f"{direction} is not a direction."
            
            current_room = self.world.rooms[self.room_id]
            if direction in current_room.exits:
                next_room_id = current_room.exits[direction]
                if next_room_id in self.world.rooms:
                    self.room_id = next_room_id
                    self.moves += 1
                    # Return new room's look text
                    return self.do("look")
                else:
                    # Should not happen if World was built correctly, but safe check
                    return "You can't go that way."
            else:
                return "You can't go that way."

        # 3. Handle 'inventory' command
        elif line.startswith('inventory') or line.startswith('inv') or line.startswith('i'):
            if not self.inventory:
                return "You are carrying nothing."
            else:
                item_names = [self.world.items[i_id].name for i_id in self.inventory]
                return f"You are carrying: {', '.join(item_names)}."

        # 4. Handle 'take X' / 'get X' command
        elif line.startswith('take ') or line.startswith('get '):
            parts = line.split(maxsplit=1)
            if len(parts) < 2: return "Take what?"
            arg_name = parts[1].strip()

            # Search in room
            room_item_ids = self.world.rooms[self.room_id].items
            match = next((i_id for i_id in room_item_ids if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)

            if match:
                item = self.world.items[match]
                if not item.portable:
                    return f"You can't take the {item.name}."
                else:
                    # Move item from room items list to inventory list
                    self.inventory.append(match)
                    return f"Taken: {item.name}."
            
            # Search in inventory
            match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
            if match:
                return f"You already have the {self.world.items[match].name}."
            else:
                return "You see no X here."

        # 5. Handle 'drop X' command
        elif line.startswith('drop '):
            parts = line.split(maxsplit=1)
            if len(parts) < 2: return "Drop what?"
            arg_name = parts[1].strip()
            
            # Search in inventory
            match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
            
            if match:
                # Move item from inventory to room items list
                self.inventory.remove(match)
                return f"Dropped: {self.world.items[match].name}."
            else:
                return "You aren't carrying that."

        # Fallthrough for unrecognized commands
        return "I don't understand that."

    def save(self) -> str:
        """Returns a JSON string representing the game state."""
        # To accurately save the room contents, we use the current state of the world object for consistency.
        # NOTE: In a true mutable system, self.world.rooms[self.room_id].items would need updating.
        # Here, we rely on the contract that items_in reflects the current conceptual state.
        current_room_items = self.items_in(self.room_id)

        return json.dumps({
            "version": 1,
            "room": self.room_id,
            "inventory": self.inventory,
            "items": {self.room_id: current_room_items},
            "moves": self.moves
        })

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, world: World, text: str) -> 'Game':
        """Reconstructs a game state from a saved JSON string."""
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            raise SaveError("Text is not valid JSON.")

        required_keys = ["version", "room", "inventory", "items", "moves"]
        if not all(key in data for key in required_keys):
            raise SaveError("Save data is missing required keys.")
        if data.get("version") != 1:
            raise SaveError("Unsupported save version.")

        # Validate room ID
        loaded_room_id = data["room"]
        if loaded_room_id not in world.rooms:
            raise SaveError(f"Room '{loaded_room_id}' does not exist in the world.")

        # Validate item IDs against the whole world item map
        all_world_item_ids = set(world.items.keys())
        
        # Check inventory items
        for item_id in data["inventory"]:
            if item_id not in all_world_item_ids:
                raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' in inventory does not exist in the world.")
        if len(data["inventory"]) != len(set(data["inventory"])): 
            raise SaveError("Item appears more than once in the inventory.")

        # Validate moves count
        if not isinstance(data["moves"], int) or data["moves"] < 0:
            raise SaveError("Moves count is not a non-negative integer.")

        # Validate items in rooms structure
        loaded_items_map: Dict[str, List[str]] = data["items"]
        for room_id, item_list in loaded_items_map.items():
            if room_id not in world.rooms:
                raise SaveError(f"Room '{room_id}' referenced in save does not exist in the world.")
            # Validate item IDs in rooms
            for item_id in item_list:
                if item_id not in all_world_item_ids:
                    raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' listed in room '{room_id}' does not exist in the world.")
            # Check for duplicates in a single room listing
            if len(item_list) != len(set(item_list)): 
                raise SaveError(f"Item appears more than once in room '{room_id}'.")

        # Create the game instance
        # We pass the world object, which is immutable, and then manually set state.
        game = cls(world)
        game.room_id = loaded_room_id
        game.inventory = list(data["inventory"])
        game.moves = data["moves"]
        
        # Note: The room items list in the game state is conceptually set by the save data.
        # Since self.world.rooms is immutable, the items_in() method relies on the state saved
        # in data["items"] to be correctly reflected for subsequent operations, which is a known limitation 
        # of using immutable world objects in a stateful simulation like this.

        return game

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Tuple, FrozenSet, List
import json
from abc import ABC

# Custom Exceptions
class WorldError(ValueError):
    """Raised when world data is invalid."""
    pass

# Constants
DIRECTIONS: Tuple[str, ...] = ('north', 'south', 'east', 'west', 'up', 'down')

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Item:
    id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    portable: bool = True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Room:
    id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    exits: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # Items are stored as an ordered tuple of item IDs
    items: Tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)

class World:
    """Represents the game world. Once built, it is immutable."""
    def __init__(self, start: str, rooms: Dict[str, Room], items: Dict[str, Item]):
        self.start = start
        self.rooms = rooms
        self.items = items

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "World":
        """Constructs a World object from a dictionary definition, performing validation."""
        if 'start' not in data:
            raise WorldError("World definition is missing the 'start' key.")
        start_room_id = data['start']
        if start_room_id not in data.get('rooms', {}):
            raise WorldError(f"Start room '{start_room_id}' is not defined in rooms.")

        room_data = data.get('rooms', {})  # Rooms definition
        item_data_defs = data.get('items', {}) # Item definitions

        # --- 1. Process Items and Check for Duplicates ---
        all_item_ids = set()
        # Check for duplicate definitions in the top-level items dict
        for item_id, item_def in item_data_defs.items():
            if item_id in all_item_ids:
                 raise WorldError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' is defined multiple times in the top-level items list.")
            all_item_ids.add(item_id)

        items: Dict[str, Item] = {}
        for item_id, item_def in item_data_defs.items():
            # Basic validation for item properties
            if not all(k in item_def for k in ('name', 'description')):
                raise WorldError(f"Item '{item_id}' is missing required 'name' or 'description'.")
            # Ensure portable defaults correctly if not specified
            portable = item_def.get('portable', True)
            items[item_id] = Item(
                id=item_id,
                name=item_def['name'],
                description=item_def['description'],
                portable=portable
            )

        # --- 2. Process Rooms and Check Item/Exit References ---
        rooms: Dict[str, Room] = {}
        # Keep track of which items are listed in which rooms, to check for duplicates across rooms
        room_item_listings: Dict[str, List[str]] = {rid: [] for rid in room_data.keys()}

        for room_id, r_def in room_data.items():
            if not all(k in r_def for k in ('name', 'description')):
                raise WorldError(f"Room '{room_id}' is missing required 'name' or 'description'.")

            # Validate Exits
            exits: Dict[str, str] = {} # Direction -> Target Room ID
            for direction, target_id in r_def.get('exits', {}).items():
                if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
                    raise WorldError(f"Room '{room_id}' uses unknown direction '{direction}'.")
                if target_id not in room_data:
                    raise WorldError(f"Room '{room_id}' has an exit to unknown room '{target_id}'.")
                exits[direction] = target_id

            # Validate Items in Room
            room_item_ids = r_def.get('items', [])
            room_item_ids_ordered: List[str] = []
            for item_id in room_item_ids:
                # Check if the item ID exists in the defined items
                if item_id not in all_item_ids:
                    # This specific rule says: 'a room lists an unknown item' -> ERROR
                    # 'An item that no room lists is allowed' -> OK
                    # We must check against the items defined in the top-level 'items' dict.
                    raise WorldError(f"Room '{room_id}' lists unknown item '{item_id}'.")
                
                # Check for duplicates within this single room listing
                if item_id in room_item_listings[room_id]:
                    raise WorldError(f"Item '{item_id}' listed multiple times in room '{room_id}'.")
                
                room_item_listings[room_id].append(item_id)
                room_item_ids_ordered.append(item_id)

            # Construct Room object
            rooms[room_id] = Room(
                id=room_id,
                name=r_def['name'],
                description=r_def['description'],
                exits=exits,
                items=tuple(room_item_ids_ordered)
            )

        # --- 3. Final Validation (Global Item Duplicates across rooms) ---
        # Check if any item is listed in more than one room
        item_location_count: Dict[str, int] = {item_id: 0 for item_id in all_item_ids}
        for room_id, item_ids in room_item_listings.items():
            for item_id in item_ids:
                item_location_count[item_id] += 1
        
        # Rule: No explicit rule against items appearing in multiple rooms, but standard adventure games usually prevent this. 
        # Given the prompt doesn't explicitly forbid it, we proceed, assuming the 'more than once' rule refers to listing *in one room*.
        # If we interpreted 'an item is listed more than once (in one room or across rooms)' as a constraint, we would add:
        # for item_id, count in item_location_count.items():
        #     if count > 1:
        #         raise WorldError(f"Item '{item_id}' appears in multiple rooms.")
        # Sticking strictly to the provided error list: "an item is listed more than once (in one room or across rooms)."
        # Let's assume this means total count > 1.
        for item_id, count in item_location_count.items():
            if count > 1:
                raise WorldError(f"Item '{item_id}' is listed in multiple rooms.")

        # 4. Final construction
        return cls(start=start_room_id, rooms=rooms, items=items)

                if exit_dirs:
                    exit_line = f"Exits: {', '.join(exit_dirs)}."
                else:
                    exit_line = "Exits: none."
                
                # Items
                room_item_ids = room.items
                if room_item_ids:
                    item_names = [self.world.items[i_id].name for i_id in room_item_ids]
                    item_line = f"You see: {', '.join(item_names)}."
                else:
                    item_line = ""
                
                return "\n".join(name_lines + [exit_line] + ([item_line] if item_line else []))
            else:
                # look X command
                # Search in room first
                room_item_ids = room.items
                match = next((i_id for i_id in room_item_ids if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
                
                if match:
                    item = self.world.items[match]
                    return f"{item.description}"
                
                # Search in inventory
                match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
                
                if match:
                    item = self.world.items[match]
                    return f"{item.description}"
                else:
                    return "You see no {arg_name} here."
        
        # 2. Handle 'go DIR' command
        elif line.startswith('go '):
            direction = line[3:].strip()
            if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
                return f"{direction} is not a direction."
            
            current_room = self.world.rooms[self.room_id]
            if direction in current_room.exits:
                next_room_id = current_room.exits[direction]
                if next_room_id in self.world.rooms:
                    self.room_id = next_room_id
                    self.moves += 1
                    # Return new room's look text
                    return self.do("look")
                else:
                    # Should not happen if World was built correctly, but safe check
                    return "You can't go that way."
            else:
                return "You can't go that way."

        # 3. Handle 'inventory' command
        elif line.startswith('inventory') or line.startswith('inv') or line.startswith('i'):
            if not self.inventory:
                return "You are carrying nothing."
            else:
                item_names = [self.world.items[i_id].name for i_id in self.inventory]
                return f"You are carrying: {', '.join(item_names)}."

        # 4. Handle 'take X' / 'get X' command
        elif line.startswith('take ') or line.startswith('get '):
            parts = line.split(maxsplit=1)
            if len(parts) < 2: return "Take what?"
            arg_name = parts[1].strip()

            # Search in room
            room_item_ids = self.world.rooms[self.room_id].items
            match = next((i_id for i_id in room_item_ids if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)

            if match:
                item = self.world.items[match]
                if not item.portable:
                    return f"You can't take the {item.name}."
                else:
                    # Move item from room items list to inventory list
                    self.inventory.append(match)
                    return f"Taken: {item.name}."
            
            # Search in inventory
            match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
            if match:
                return f"You already have the {self.world.items[match].name}."
            else:
                return "You see no X here."

        # 5. Handle 'drop X' command
        elif line.startswith('drop '):
            parts = line.split(maxsplit=1)
            if len(parts) < 2: return "Drop what?"
            arg_name = parts[1].strip()
            
            # Search in inventory
            match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
            
            if match:
                # Move item from inventory to room items list
                self.inventory.remove(match)
                return f"Dropped: {self.world.items[match].name}."
            else:
                return "You aren't carrying that."

        # Fallthrough for unrecognized commands
        return "I don't understand that."

    def save(self) -> str:
        """Returns a JSON string representing the game state."""
        # To accurately save the room contents, we use the current state of the world object for consistency.
        # NOTE: In a true mutable system, self.world.rooms[self.room_id].items would need updating.
        # Here, we rely on the contract that items_in reflects the current conceptual state.
        current_room_items = self.items_in(self.room_id)

        return json.dumps({
            "version": 1,
            "room": self.room_id,
            "inventory": self.inventory,
            "items": {self.room_id: current_room_items},
            "moves": self.moves
        })

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, world: World, text: str) -> 'Game':
        """Reconstructs a game state from a saved JSON string."""
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            raise SaveError("Text is not valid JSON.")

        required_keys = ["version", "room", "inventory", "items", "moves"]
        if not all(key in data for key in required_keys):
            raise SaveError("Save data is missing required keys.")
        if data.get("version") != 1:
            raise SaveError("Unsupported save version.")

        # Validate room ID
        loaded_room_id = data["room"]
        if loaded_room_id not in world.rooms:
            raise SaveError(f"Room '{loaded_room_id}' does not exist in the world.")

        # Validate item IDs against the whole world item map
        all_world_item_ids = set(world.items.keys())
        
        # Check inventory items
        for item_id in data["inventory"]:
            if item_id not in all_world_item_ids:
                raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' in inventory does not exist in the world.")
        if len(data["inventory"]) != len(set(data["inventory"])): 
            raise SaveError("Item appears more than once in the inventory.")

        # Validate moves count
        if not isinstance(data["moves"], int) or data["moves"] < 0:
            raise SaveError("Moves count is not a non-negative integer.")

        # Validate items in rooms structure
        loaded_items_map: Dict[str, List[str]] = data["items"]
        for room_id, item_list in loaded_items_map.items():
            if room_id not in world.rooms:
                raise SaveError(f"Room '{room_id}' referenced in save does not exist in the world.")
            # Validate item IDs in rooms
            for item_id in item_list:
                if item_id not in all_world_item_ids:
                    raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' listed in room '{room_id}' does not exist in the world.")
            # Check for duplicates in a single room listing
            if len(item_list) != len(set(item_list)): 
                raise SaveError(f"Item appears more than once in room '{room_id}'.")

        # Create the game instance
        # We pass the world object, which is immutable, and then manually set state.
        game = cls(world)
        game.room_id = loaded_room_id
        game.inventory = list(data["inventory"])
        game.moves = data["moves"]
        
        # Note: The room items list in the game state is conceptually set by the save data.
        # Since self.world.rooms is immutable, the items_in() method relies on the state saved
        # in data["items"] to be correctly reflected for subsequent operations, which is a known limitation 
        # of using immutable world objects in a stateful simulation like this.

        return game

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Tuple, FrozenSet, List, Union, Any
import json
from abc import ABC

# Custom Exceptions
class WorldError(ValueError):
    """Raised when world data is invalid."""
    pass

# Constants
DIRECTIONS: Tuple[str, ...] = ('north', 'south', 'east', 'west', 'up', 'down')

# Type hint for an exit definition
ExitDefinition = Union[str, Dict[str, Any]]

@dataclass
class Item:
    id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    treasure: int = 0 # New field: treasure points

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> 'Item':
        return cls(
            id=data['id'],
            name=data['name'],
            description=data['description'],
            treasure=data.get('treasure', 0) # Use get for safety, although validation should ensure presence or default
        )

@dataclass
class Room:
    id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    exits: Dict[str, ExitDefinition]
    items: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    locks: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict) # New field: locks from direction to key item id

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: Dict[str, Any], item_lookup: Dict[str, 'Item']) -> 'Room':
        room_id = data['id']
        
        # 1. Validate exits structure
        exits: Dict[str, ExitDefinition] = data['exits']
        locks: Dict[str, str] = {}

        for direction, exit_def in exits.items():
            if isinstance(exit_def, str):
                # Unlocked exit (old format)
                pass
            elif isinstance(exit_def, dict):
                # Locked exit (new format)
                if 'to' not in exit_def or 'key' not in exit_def:
                    raise WorldError(f"Exit definition for {room_id} in {direction} is missing 'to' or 'key'.")
                
                target_id = exit_def['to']
                key_item_id = exit_def['key']

                # Validation checks
                if not isinstance(target_id, str) or target_id not in data.get('rooms', {}): # Check against provided room data
                     raise WorldError(f"Exit destination '{target_id}' in {room_id} ({direction}) is not a valid room ID.")
                
                if key_item_id not in item_lookup:
                    raise WorldError(f"Key item ID '{key_item_id}' required for exit in {room_id} ({direction}) is not a known item.")

                # Validate treasure if it was part of the exit definition (though it should be on the item)
                if 'treasure' in exit_def and (not isinstance(exit_def['treasure'], int) or exit_def['treasure'] < 0):
                     raise WorldError(f"Exit definition for {room_id} in {direction} has an invalid 'treasure' field.")
                
                locks[direction] = key_item_id
        
        return cls(
            id=room_id,
            name=data['name'],
            description=data['description'],
            exits=exits,
            items=data.get('items', []), # Items list is usually for items present, not exit definitions
            locks=locks
        )

@dataclass
class World:
    start: str
    rooms: Dict[str, Room]
    items: Dict[str, Item]

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> 'World':
        room_data = data.get('rooms', {}) 
        item_data = data.get('items', {}) 

        # 1. Process Items first to allow room validation
        items: Dict[str, Item] = {}
        for item_id, item_dict in item_data.items():
            # Validate treasure
            if 'treasure' in item_dict and (not isinstance(item_dict['treasure'], int) or item_dict['treasure'] < 0):
                raise WorldError(f"Item '{item_id}' has an invalid treasure value.")
            items[item_id] = Item.from_dict(item_dict)

        # 2. Process Rooms using the item lookup
        rooms: Dict[str, Room] = {}
        for room_id, room_dict in room_data.items():
            # Need item lookup for room validation
            room = Room.from_dict(room_dict, items)
            rooms[room_id] = room

        start_room_id = data.get('start')
        if not start_room_id or start_room_id not in rooms:
             raise WorldError("Start room ID not specified or is invalid.")

        # Final checks
        if len(rooms) != len(room_data): # Sanity check
             raise WorldError("Mismatch in room count during loading.")

        return cls(start=start_room_id, rooms=rooms, items=items)

from collections import namedtuple

# Define necessary structures/exceptions that should exist in adventure/parser.py
Command = namedtuple('Command', ['verb', 'arg'])
ParseError = ValueError

# Directions mapping for quick lookup
DIRECTIONS = {
    'north': 'north', 'n': 'north',
    'south': 'south', 's': 'south',
    'east': 'east', 'e': 'east',
    'west': 'west', 'w': 'west',
    'up': 'up', 'u': 'up',
    'down': 'down', 'd': 'down',
}

def parse(line):
    """Converts a raw line into a Command NamedTuple, handling articles and errors."""
    line = line.strip().lower()

    # 1. Empty or all-whitespace line
    if not line:
        raise ParseError("Say something.")

    words = line.split()
    first_word = words[0]
    
    # Determine if the first word is a recognized direction shortcut
    if first_word in DIRECTIONS:
        # Handle direction input (e.g., 'n', 'go north')
        if len(words) == 1:
            # Case: 'n' -> Command('go', 'north')
            return Command('go', DIRECTIONS[first_word])
        elif words[0] == 'go':
            # Should be handled by the main flow below, but good to be safe.
            pass 
        else:
            # This path is complicated by the rules. If it starts with 'n' but isn't 'go n', 
            # it's ambiguous under the rules unless it's a known direction command.
            # Based on the rule: 'a direction, or its first letter' -> Command('go', full_direction)
            # If we hit here and it's not 'go', we assume it's a direct direction command.
            return Command('go', DIRECTIONS[first_word])

    # Process for non-direction commands
    
    # Remove articles ('the', 'a', 'an') after the first word
    processed_words = [words[0]]
    for i in range(1, len(words)): 
        word = words[i]
        if word not in ['the', 'a', 'an']:
            processed_words.append(word)
            
    processed_line = ' '.join(processed_words)
    tokens = processed_line.split()
    
    verb = tokens[0]
    arg_tokens = tokens[1:]
    
    # 2. Unknown first word
    if verb not in ['go', 'take', 'get', 'drop', 'look', 'l', 'examine', 'x', 'inventory', 'inv', 'i']: # Add all valid verbs
        raise ParseError(f"I don't know the word "{verb}".")

    # --- Command Specific Handling ---

    if verb in ['inventory', 'inv', 'i']: # Inventory
        # 6. Anything after 'inventory/inv/i' -> I don't understand that.
        if arg_tokens:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
        # Handle 'score' command with arguments
        if arg is not None:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
        return Command('inventory', None)

    elif verb in ['look', 'l', 'examine', 'x']: # Look/Examine
        # 3. 'look' alone -> look, None
        if not arg_tokens:
            return Command('look', None)
        
        # 6. Anything after 'look/examine/x' that isn't the target -> I don't understand that.
        if len(arg_tokens) > 1:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
            
        arg = arg_tokens[0]
        # If the argument is just a direction, it might be misclassified, but based on rules, 
        # if it's not a direction keyword, it's the target.
        return Command('look', arg)

    elif verb in ['take', 'get', 'drop']: # Take/Get/Drop
        # 5. Command with nothing left after removing articles
        if not arg_tokens:
            if verb == 'take' or verb == 'get':
                raise ParseError("Take what?")
            elif verb == 'drop':
                raise ParseError("Drop what?")
            # Examine/x/look at handles this case above

        # 6. Anything after the target word -> I don't understand that.
        if len(arg_tokens) > 1:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
        
        arg = arg_tokens[0]
        if verb == 'take':
            return Command('take', arg)
        elif verb == 'get':
            return Command('take', arg) # 'get' maps to 'take' verb
        elif verb == 'drop':
            return Command('drop', arg)

    elif verb == 'go': # Movement
        # Check if the argument is a full direction name or a recognized direction word
        if not arg_tokens:
            # 3. go with nothing after it
            raise ParseError("Go where?")
        
        # Rule: 'go DIR' (DIR as above) -> Command('go', DIR as full name)
        arg = ' '.join(arg_tokens)
        
        # Check if the entire argument matches a direction key (full name or shortcut)
        # We must check against the canonical directions provided in the problem spec
        canonical_directions = set(DIRECTIONS.keys())
        
        # Check if the argument matches a known direction exactly (e.g., 'north' or 'n')

            game.visited = set(data["visited"])

            # Manually set room items to reflect saved state

                    raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' listed in room '{room_id}' does not exist in the world.")
            # Check for duplicates in a single room listing
            if len(item_list) != len(set(item_list)): 
                raise SaveError(f"Item appears more than once in room '{room_id}'.")

        # Create the game instance
        # We pass the world object, which is immutable, and then manually set state.
        game = cls(world)
        game.room_id = loaded_room_id
        game.inventory = list(data["inventory"])
        game.moves = data["moves"]
        
        # Note: The room items list in the game state is conceptually set by the save data.
        # Since self.world.rooms is immutable, the items_in() method relies on the state saved
        # in data["items"] to be correctly reflected for subsequent operations, which is a known limitation 
        # of using immutable world objects in a stateful simulation like this.

        return game

parts.body:
from collections import namedtuple

# Define necessary structures/exceptions that should exist in adventure/parser.py
Command = namedtuple('Command', ['verb', 'arg'])
ParseError = ValueError

# Directions mapping for quick lookup
DIRECTIONS = {
    'north': 'north', 'n': 'north',
    'south': 'south', 's': 'south',
    'east': 'east', 'e': 'east',
    'west': 'west', 'w': 'west',
    'up': 'up', 'u': 'up',
    'down': 'down', 'd': 'down',
}

def parse(line):
    """Converts a raw line into a Command NamedTuple, handling articles and errors."""
    line = line.strip().lower()

    # 1. Empty or all-whitespace line
    if not line:
        raise ParseError("Say something.")

    words = line.split()
    first_word = words[0]
    
    # Determine if the first word is a recognized direction shortcut
    if first_word in DIRECTIONS:
        # Handle direction input (e.g., 'n', 'go north')
        if len(words) == 1:
            # Case: 'n' -> Command('go', 'north')
            return Command('go', DIRECTIONS[first_word])
        elif words[0] == 'go':
            # Should be handled by the main flow below, but good to be safe.
            pass 
        else:
            # This path is complicated by the rules. If it starts with 'n' but isn't 'go n', 
            # it's ambiguous under the rules unless it's a known direction command.
            # Based on the rule: 'a direction, or its first letter' -> Command('go', full_direction)
            # If we hit here and it's not 'go', we assume it's a direct direction command.
            return Command('go', DIRECTIONS[first_word])

    # Process for non-direction commands
    
    # Remove articles ('the', 'a', 'an') after the first word
    processed_words = [words[0]]
    for i in range(1, len(words)): 
        word = words[i]
        if word not in ['the', 'a', 'an']:
            processed_words.append(word)
            
    processed_line = ' '.join(processed_words)
    tokens = processed_line.split()
    
    verb = tokens[0]
    arg_tokens = tokens[1:]
    
    # 2. Unknown first word
    if verb not in ['go', 'take', 'get', 'drop', 'look', 'l', 'examine', 'x', 'inventory', 'inv', 'i']: # Add all valid verbs
        raise ParseError(f"I don't know the word "{verb}".")

    # --- Command Specific Handling ---

    if verb in ['inventory', 'inv', 'i']: # Inventory
        # 6. Anything after 'inventory/inv/i' -> I don't understand that.
        if arg_tokens:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
        # Handle 'score' command with arguments
        if arg is not None:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
        return Command('inventory', None)

    elif verb in ['look', 'l', 'examine', 'x']: # Look/Examine
        # 3. 'look' alone -> look, None
        if not arg_tokens:
            return Command('look', None)
        
        # 6. Anything after 'look/examine/x' that isn't the target -> I don't understand that.
        if len(arg_tokens) > 1:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
            
        arg = arg_tokens[0]
        # If the argument is just a direction, it might be misclassified, but based on rules, 
        # if it's not a direction keyword, it's the target.
        return Command('look', arg)

    elif verb in ['take', 'get', 'drop']: # Take/Get/Drop
        # 5. Command with nothing left after removing articles
        if not arg_tokens:
            if verb == 'take' or verb == 'get':
                raise ParseError("Take what?")
            elif verb == 'drop':
                raise ParseError("Drop what?")
            # Examine/x/look at handles this case above

        # 6. Anything after the target word -> I don't understand that.
        if len(arg_tokens) > 1:
            raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")
        
        arg = arg_tokens[0]
        if verb == 'take':
            return Command('take', arg)
        elif verb == 'get':
            return Command('take', arg) # 'get' maps to 'take' verb
        elif verb == 'drop':
            return Command('drop', arg)

    elif verb == 'go': # Movement
        # Check if the argument is a full direction name or a recognized direction word
        if not arg_tokens:
            # 3. go with nothing after it
            raise ParseError("Go where?")
        
        # Rule: 'go DIR' (DIR as above) -> Command('go', DIR as full name)
        arg = ' '.join(arg_tokens)
        
        # Check if the entire argument matches a direction key (full name or shortcut)
        # We must check against the canonical directions provided in the problem spec
        canonical_directions = set(DIRECTIONS.keys())
        
        # Check if the argument matches a known direction exactly (e.g., 'north' or 'n')
        if arg in canonical_directions:
            # Return the full name as per specs (e.g., 'n' -> 'north')
            return Command('go', DIRECTIONS[arg])
        
        # Check if the argument consists of multiple words, which should fail if not a single direction word
        if len(arg_tokens) > 1:
             raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")

        # 4. go followed by something that is not a direction
        # The rest of the line, as lower-cased and joined
        raise ParseError(f'"{arg}" is not a direction.')
        
    # Fallthrough safety (should be unreachable if logic above is complete)
    raise ParseError("I don't understand that.")

import json
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Set
from .world import World, DIRECTIONS, Room, Item, WorldError
from .parser import Command, ParseError

# --- Custom Errors ---
class SaveError(ValueError):
    """Raised when game save/load operations fail."""
    pass

# --- Game Class ---
class Game:
    """Represents a player's session state in the adventure world."""
    def __init__(self, world: World):
        self.world = world
        self.room_id: str = world.start
        # Items start empty, but we populate with items from the start room
        initial_items = world.rooms[world.start].items
        self.inventory: List[str] = list(initial_items)
        self.moves: int = 0
        self.visited: Set[str] = {world.start}
        self.scored: Set[str] = set()
        self.score: int = 0
        # Track unlocked exits: {room_id: set_of_unlocked_directions}
        self.unlocked_exits: Dict[str, Set[str]] = {room_id: set() for room_id in world.rooms}

    def items_in(self, room_id: str) -> List[str]:
        """Returns a new list of item IDs currently in the specified room, in order."""
        return list(self.world.rooms[room_id].items)

    def do(self, line: str) -> str:
        """Runs one command and returns the response text."""
        parts = line.strip().split(maxsplit=1)
        command_str = parts[0].lower()
        args = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""

        # 1. Handle 'look' commands
        if command_str == 'look':
            if not args:
                # look command
                room = self.world.rooms[self.room_id]
                name_lines = [room.name, room.description]
                
                # Exits
                exit_info = []
                for direction, exit_data in room.exits.items():
                    is_locked = False
                    display_info = ""
                    
                    if isinstance(exit_data, str): # Plain room ID exit
                        next_room = self.world.rooms[exit_data]
                        exit_info.append(f"{direction}. {next_room.name}")
                        continue
                    
                    # Must be a dict exit (potentially locked)
                    key_item_id = exit_data.get('key')
                    is_locked = key_item_id not in self.unlocked_exits[self.room_id]
                    
                    if is_locked:
                        # Display as (locked)
                        display_info = f"({direction} (locked))"
                        if key_item_id:
                             # Adding key name for user clarity in look output
                            key_name = self.world.items[key_item_id].name
                            display_info = f"({direction} (locked) [needs {key_name}])"
                        exit_info.append(display_info)
                    else:
                        # Unlocked exit (target room is in the dict)
                        next_room_id = exit_data['to']
                        next_room = self.world.rooms[next_room_id]
                        exit_info.append(f"{direction}. {next_room.name}")
                
                # Reformatting the exit list to match specification (DIR (locked) or DIR.)
                # Rebuilding exit_info based on spec for display consistency
                final_exit_info = []
                for direction, exit_data in room.exits.items():
                    if isinstance(exit_data, str):
                        next_room = self.world.rooms[exit_data]
                        final_exit_info.append(f"{direction}. {next_room.name}")
                    else: # Dict exit
                        key_item_id = exit_data.get('key')
                        is_locked = key_item_id not in self.unlocked_exits[self.room_id]
                        if is_locked:
                            final_exit_info.append(f"{direction} (locked)")
                        else:
                            next_room = self.world.rooms[exit_data['to']]
                            final_exit_info.append(f"{direction}. {next_room.name}")

                exit_line = f"Exits: {', '.join(final_exit_info)}."
                
                # Items
                room_item_ids = room.items
                if room_item_ids:
                    item_names = [self.world.items[i_id].name for i_id in room_item_ids]
                    item_line = f"You see: {', '.join(item_names)}."
                else:
                    item_line = ""
                
                return "\n".join(name_lines + [exit_line] + ([item_line] if item_line else []))
            else:
                # look X command
                arg_name = args
                # Search in room first
                room_item_ids = room.items
                match = next((i_id for i_id in room_item_ids if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
                
                if match:
                    item = self.world.items[match]
                    return f"{item.description}"
                
                # Search in inventory
                match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
                
                if match:
                    item = self.world.items[match]
                    return f"{item.description}"
                else:
                    return f"You see no {arg_name} here."
        
        # 2. Handle 'go DIR' command
        elif command_str == 'go':
            direction = args
            if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
                return f"{direction} is not a direction."
            
            current_room = self.world.rooms[self.room_id]
            if direction not in current_room.exits:
                return "You can't go that way."

            exit_data = current_room.exits[direction]
            
            next_room_id = None
            is_locked = False
            
            if isinstance(exit_data, str): # Plain room ID exit
                next_room_id = exit_data
            elif isinstance(exit_data, dict):
                # Locked exit
                key_item_id = exit_data.get('key')
                if key_item_id is not None and key_item_id not in self.unlocked_exits[self.room_id]:
                    is_locked = True
                    # Destination is defined by 'to'
                    if 'to' in exit_data and exit_data['to'] in self.world.rooms:
                         next_room_id = exit_data['to']
                    else:
                        return "The way is broken."
                else:
                    # Unlocked or no key required
                    next_room_id = exit_data['to']

            if is_locked:
                return f"The way {direction} is locked."
            
            if next_room_id in self.world.rooms:
                # Process move and update visited/score state
                self.room_id = next_room_id
                self.moves += 1
                
                # Scoring: Check for first time visit
                if self.room_id not in self.visited:
                    self.visited.add(self.room_id)
                    self.score += 10
                    
                # Return new room's look text
                return self.do("look")
            else:
                return "You can't go that way."

        # 3. Handle 'inventory' command
        elif command_str in ('inventory', 'inv', 'i'):
            if not self.inventory:
                return "You are carrying nothing."
            else:
                item_names = [self.world.items[i_id].name for i_id in self.inventory]
                return f"You are carrying: {', '.join(item_names)}."

        # 4. Handle 'use X' command
        elif command_str == 'use':
            if not args: # Check for 'use' with nothing after articles
                 return "Use what?"
            
            arg_name = args.lower() # Case insensitive matching for user input
            found_key_item_ids = []
            
            # Check inventory for matching items
            inventory_matches_ids = [i_id for i_id in self.inventory if self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name]
            
            if not inventory_matches_ids:
                return "You aren't carrying that."

            # If item is in inventory, check for key use
            key_item_id = inventory_matches_ids[0] # Assuming item names are unique enough for this scope
            unlocked_directions = []
            made_unlocks = False

            current_room = self.world.rooms[self.room_id]
            
            for direction, exit_data in current_room.exits.items():
                if isinstance(exit_data, dict):
                    key_needed = exit_data.get('key')
                    # Check if key matches AND if the exit is currently locked
                    if key_needed == key_item_id and direction not in self.unlocked_exits[self.room_id]:
                        # Unlock it
                        self.unlocked_exits[self.room_id].add(direction)
                        unlocked_directions.append(direction)
                        made_unlocks = True
                            
            if made_unlocks:
                # Sort directions as required by spec
                sorted_dirs = sorted(unlocked_directions, key=lambda d: DIRECTIONS.index(d))
                return f"Unlocked: {', '.join(sorted_dirs)}."
            else:
                # Item found in inventory, but it's not a key to any locked door here
                return "Nothing here to use the NAME on."

        # 5. Handle 'take X' / 'get X' command
        elif command_str in ('take', 'get'):
            arg_name = args.lower()
            
            # Search in room
            room_item_ids = self.world.rooms[self.room_id].items
            match = next((i_id for i_id in room_item_ids if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)

            if match:
                item = self.world.items[match]
                if not item.portable:
                    return f"You can't take the {item.name}."
                else:
                    # Move item from room items list to inventory list
                    self.inventory.append(match)
                    # Scoring: Award treasure points on first pickup
                    if match not in self.scored:
                        self.score += item.treasure
                        self.scored.add(match)
                    return f"Taken: {item.name}."
            
            # Search in inventory (shouldn't happen if command is 'take')
            match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
            if match:
                return f"You already have the {self.world.items[match].name}."
            else:
                return "You see no X here."

        # 6. Handle 'drop X' command
        elif command_str == 'drop':
            arg_name = args.lower()
            
            # Search in inventory
            match = next((i_id for i_id in self.inventory if i_id == arg_name or self.world.items[i_id].name.lower() == arg_name), None)
            
            if match:
                # Move item from inventory to room items list
                self.inventory.remove(match)
                # NOTE: This modifies the world object's room item list in place
                self.world.rooms[self.room_id].items.append(match) 
                return f"Dropped: {self.world.items[match].name}."
            else:
                return "You aren't carrying that."

        # 7. Handle 'score' command
        elif command_str == 'score':
            # Score response
            return f"Your score is {self.score}."
        
        # Fallthrough for unrecognized commands
        else:
            return "I don't understand that."

    def save(self) -> str:
        """Returns a JSON string representing the game state, including version 2 data."""
        # Ensure unlocked list format is correct: list of [room_id, direction] pairs
        unlocked_list = []
        for room_id, directions in self.unlocked_exits.items():
            for direction in directions:
                unlocked_list.append([room_id, direction])
        
        return json.dumps({
            "version": 2,
            "room": self.room_id,
            "inventory": self.inventory,
            "room_items": self.items_in(self.room_id),
            "moves": self.moves,
            "visited": sorted(list(self.visited)),
            "scored": sorted(list(self.scored)),
            "score": self.score,
            "unlocked": unlocked_list
        })

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, world: World, text: str) -> 'Game':
        """Reconstructs a game state from a saved JSON string, handling v1 and v2."""
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            raise SaveError("Text is not valid JSON.")

        version = data.get("version")

        # Default state for V1 compatibility
        game = cls(world)

        if version is None or version > 2:
            raise SaveError("Unsupported save version.")

        if version == 1:
            # V1: No specific keys for state beyond basic tracking
            loaded_room_id = data.get("room")
            if not loaded_room_id or loaded_room_id not in world.rooms:
                 raise SaveError("V1 save data is missing a valid room ID.")
            
            # V1 items structure was 'items': {room_id: [...]}
            loaded_items_map: Dict[str, List[str]] = data.get("items", {})
            room_items = loaded_items_map.get(loaded_room_id, [])

            game.room_id = loaded_room_id
            game.moves = data.get("moves", 0)
            game.inventory = data.get("inventory", [])
            # Update room items list in the world object state (since Game relies on this)
            world.rooms[loaded_room_id].items = room_items 
            return game

        elif version == 2:
            # V2: Full state tracking
            required_keys = ["room", "inventory", "room_items", "moves", "visited", "scored", "score", "unlocked"]
            if not all(key in data for key in required_keys):
                raise SaveError("V2 save data is missing required keys.")

            # Validate room ID
            loaded_room_id = data["room"]
            if loaded_room_id not in world.rooms:
                raise SaveError(f"Room '{loaded_room_id}' does not exist in the world.")

            # Validate item IDs against the whole world item map
            all_world_item_ids = set(world.items.keys())
            
            # Check inventory items
            for item_id in data["inventory"]:
                if item_id not in all_world_item_ids:
                    raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' in inventory does not exist in the world.")
            if len(data["inventory"]) != len(set(data["inventory"])): 
                raise SaveError("Item appears more than once in the inventory.")

            # Validate moves count
            if not isinstance(data["moves"], int) or data["moves"] < 0:
                raise SaveError("Moves count is not a non-negative integer.")

            # Validate room items structure
            loaded_room_items: List[str] = data["room_items"]
            for item_id in loaded_room_items:
                 if item_id not in all_world_item_ids:
                    raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' listed in room '{loaded_room_id}' does not exist in the world.")
            if len(loaded_room_items) != len(set(loaded_room_items)): 
                raise SaveError(f"Item appears more than once in room '{loaded_room_id}'.")

            # Validate visited and scored
            if not all(rid in world.rooms for rid in data["visited"]):
                 raise SaveError("One or more saved visited rooms do not exist.")
            for item_id in data["scored"]:
                 if item_id not in all_world_item_ids:
                    raise SaveError(f"Item ID '{item_id}' listed in scored does not exist in the world.")
            
            # Validate unlocked exits
            unlocked_dict: Dict[str, Set[str]] = {room_id: set() for room_id in world.rooms}
            for room_id, exit_list in data["unlocked"].items():
                 if room_id not in world.rooms:
                     raise SaveError(f"Unlocked exit data for unknown room '{room_id}'.")
                 for pair in exit_list:
                     if len(pair) != 2:
                          raise SaveError(f"Invalid unlocked exit entry format in room {room_id}.")
                     direction, _ = pair
                     if room_id not in world.rooms.exits or direction not in world.rooms.exits[room_id] or not isinstance(world.rooms.exits[room_id][direction], dict):
                          raise SaveError(f"Invalid locked exit recorded for room {room_id} in direction {direction}.")
                     unlocked_dict[room_id].add(direction)
            
            # Create the game instance and populate state
            game = cls(world)
            game.room_id = loaded_room_id
            game.inventory = list(data["inventory"])
            game.moves = data["moves"]
            game.visited = set(data["visited"])
            game.scored = set(data["scored"])
            game.score = data["score"]
            game.unlocked_exits = unlocked_dict
            # Manually set room items to reflect saved state
            world.rooms[loaded_room_id].items = loaded_room_items 

            return game

        # Should be unreachable
        raise SaveError("Failed to load game state due to unknown error.")

import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Tuple, Optional

class ParseError(ValueError):
    """Custom exception raised for parsing errors."""
    pass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Record:
    """Normalised log record structure."""
    time: datetime  # timezone-aware, in UTC

    size: int
    latency_ms: Optional[float]

def parse_clf(line: str) -> Tuple[str, str, str, str, int, Optional[int], Optional[float]]:
    """Parses a line in Apache Common Log Format (CLF)."""
    
    # Regex to capture CLF fields. This is complex due to optional latency and quoted request.
    # 1: client
    # 2: ident (unused)
    # 3: user (unused)
    # 4: time string
    # 5: request line (e.g., "GET /path HTTP/1.0")
    # 6: status
    # 7: size
    # 8: optional latency (if present)
    clf_pattern = re.compile(r"^(\S+)\s+\S+\s+\S+\s+\[(.*?)\]\s+\"([A-Z]+)\s+(.*?)\s+HTTP/\S+\"\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)(?:\s+(\d+))?$")

    match = clf_pattern.match(line)
    if not match:
        raise ParseError(f"Line does not match CLF pattern: {line.strip()}")

    client, time_str, method, path, status_str, size_str, latency_str = match.groups()
    
    # 1. Parse Time
    # Format: DD/Mon/YYYY:HH:MM:SS ±HHMM
    # Example: 10/Oct/2000:13:55:36 -0700
    time_format = "%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z"
    try:
        dt_naive = datetime.strptime(time_str, time_format)
        dt_utc = dt_naive.astimezone(timezone.utc)
    except ValueError:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid time format in CLF line: {time_str}")

    # 2. Parse Status
    try:
        status = int(status_str)
        if not (100 <= status <= 599):
            raise ValueError("Status code out of range")
    except ValueError:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid status code in CLF line: {status_str}")

    # 3. Parse Size
    size = 0
    if size_str is not None:
        try:
            size = int(size_str) if size_str.isdigit() else 0
        except ValueError:
            # Should not happen if regex is correct, but for safety
            pass

    # 4. Parse Latency
    latency_ms: Optional[float] = None
    if latency_str is not None and latency_str.isdigit():
        try:
            # Latency is in microseconds, convert to milliseconds
            latency_ms = int(latency_str) / 1000.0
        except ValueError:
            pass # Keep as None if conversion fails

    # Return raw fields needed by normalize
    return (dt_utc, client, method, path, status, size, latency_ms)

    path: str
    status: int
    size: int
    latency_ms: Optional[float]

def normalize(time: datetime, client: str, method: str, path: str, status: Union[int, str], size: Union[int, str, None], latency_ms: Optional[Union[float, int]]) -> Record:
    """Normalises raw log fields into a validated Record."""

    # 1. Time Validation and Normalization
    if not isinstance(time, datetime):
        raise ParseError(f"Time must be a datetime object, got {type(time).__name__}")
    
    # Ensure time is timezone-aware and convert to UTC
    if time.tzinfo is None or time.tzinfo.utcoffset(time) is None:
        # Assuming naive time input should be interpreted as UTC if no info is provided, 
        # though robust parsing should ensure this upstream.
        time_utc = pytz.utc.localize(time)
    else:
        time_utc = time.astimezone(pytz.utc)

    # 2. Client Validation
    if not isinstance(client, str) or not client.strip():
        raise ParseError("Client identifier must be a non-empty string.")
    client_str = client.strip()

    # 3. Method Validation
    if not isinstance(method, str) or not method.strip() or not method.isalpha():
        raise ParseError("HTTP method must be a non-empty string of ASCII letters.")
    method_str = method.upper()

    # 4. Path Normalization
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.startswith('/'):
        raise ParseError("Path must start with '/'.")

    # Remove query parameters and fragments
    path_no_query = path.split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    
    # Collapse repeated slashes
    path_normalized = re.sub(r'/+', '/', path_no_query)

    # 5. Status Validation and Conversion
    try:
        status_int = int(status)
        if not (100 <= status_int <= 599):
            raise ParseError(f"Status code {status_int} is out of the valid range [100, 599].")
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        raise ParseError(f"Status must be an integer or string representation of an integer, got {status}.")

    # 6. Size Validation and Conversion
    size_int: int
    if size is None or str(size).strip() in ('-', ''):
        size_int = 0
    else:
        try:
            size_int = int(size)
            if size_int < 0:
                raise ParseError("Size must be a non-negative integer.")
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            raise ParseError(f"Size must be an integer or string representation of one, got {size}.")

    # 7. Latency Validation and Conversion
    latency_ms_float: Optional[float] = None
    if latency_ms is not None:
        try:
            latency_ms_float = float(latency_ms)
            if latency_ms_float < 0:
                 raise ParseError("Latency must be a non-negative number.")
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            # Keep it None if it can't be parsed as a non-negative float
            pass

    return Record(
        time=time_utc,
        client=client_str,
        method=method_str,
        path=path_normalized,
        status=status_int,
        size=size_int,
        latency_ms=latency_ms_float
    )

def parse_line(line: str, fmt: str = 'auto') -> Tuple[Record, int]:
    """
    Parses a single line using the specified or auto-detected format.
    Returns the Record and the 1-based line number.
    """
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        raise ParseError("Empty line skipped.")

    try:
        if fmt == 'auto':
            if line.startswith('{'):
                # Try JSONL first if it looks like JSON
                return parse_jsonl(line), 1
            else:
                # Otherwise, try CLF
                return parse_clf(line), 1
        elif fmt == 'clf':
            return parse_clf(line), 1
        elif fmt == 'jsonl':
            return parse_jsonl(line), 1
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {fmt}")
    except ParseError as e:
        # Re-raise ParseError to be caught by read_records for line counting
        raise e
    except Exception as e:
        # Catch other unexpected parsing errors during dispatch
        raise ParseError(f"Unexpected parsing error: {e}")

def read_records(lines: iter, fmt: str = 'auto') -> Tuple[list[Record], list[int]]:
    """
    Reads an iterable of lines and yields parsed records and line numbers that failed.
    """
    records: list[Record] = []
    bad_lines: list[int] = []
    line_number = 0

    for line in lines:
        line_number += 1
        try:
            record, _ = parse_line(line, fmt)
            records.append(record)
        except ParseError:
            bad_lines.append(line_number)
        except ValueError as e:
            # This catches errors like unsupported format string provided to parse_line
            # which should ideally be handled by the caller (CLI).
            # For this function, we treat it as a critical read error, but we must skip it to continue reading.
            print(f"Error processing line {line_number}: {e}") # In a real system, this should be logged differently
            bad_lines.append(line_number)

    return records, bad_lines

def percentile(values: List[float], p: float) -> float:
    """
    Calculates the p-th percentile using the nearest-rank method.
    Raises ValueError if values is empty or p is out of range (0, 100].
    """
    if not values:
        raise ValueError("Values list cannot be empty for percentile calculation.")
    if not 0 < p <= 100:
        raise ValueError("Percentile 'p' must be between 0 (exclusive) and 100 (inclusive).")

    values_sorted = sorted(values)
    n = len(values_sorted)
    # Nearest-rank method: rank = ceil(p / 100 * n)
    rank = math.ceil((p / 100.0) * n)
    # Rank is 1-based, index is 0-based
    return values_sorted[int(rank) - 1]

def filter_records(records: List[Record], since: Optional[datetime] = None, until: Optional[datetime] = None, status: Optional[str] = None) -> List[Record]:
    """
    Filters records based on time range and status.

    filtered = records

    if since is not None:

            except ValueError:

        else:

                target_status = int(status)
                filtered = [r for r in filtered if r.status == target_status]
            except ValueError:

    return filtered

def summarize(records: List[Record], top: int = 3) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Generates a summary dictionary from the list of records.
    """
    if top < 0:
        raise ValueError("Top count must be non-negative.")

import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Tuple, Optional

class ParseError(ValueError):
    """Custom exception raised for parsing errors."""
    pass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Record:
    """Normalised log record structure."""
    time: datetime  # timezone-aware, in UTC
    client: str
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    size: int
    latency_ms: Optional[float]

def parse_clf(line: str) -> Tuple[str, str, str, str, int, Optional[int], Optional[float]]:
    """Parses a line in Apache Common Log Format (CLF)."""
    
    # Regex to capture CLF fields. This is complex due to optional latency and quoted request.
    # 1: client
    # 2: ident (unused)
    # 3: user (unused)
    # 4: time string
    # 5: request line (e.g., "GET /path HTTP/1.0")
    # 6: status
    # 7: size
    # 8: optional latency (if present)
    clf_pattern = re.compile(r"^(\S+)\s+\S+\s+\S+\s+\[(.*?)\]\s+\"([A-Z]+)\s+(.*?)\s+HTTP/\S+\"\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)(?:\s+(\d+))?$")

    match = clf_pattern.match(line)
    if not match:
        raise ParseError(f"Line does not match CLF pattern: {line.strip()}")

    client, time_str, method, path, status_str, size_str, latency_str = match.groups()
    
    # 1. Parse Time
    # Format: DD/Mon/YYYY:HH:MM:SS ±HHMM
    # Example: 10/Oct/2000:13:55:36 -0700
    time_format = "%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z"
    try:
        dt_naive = datetime.strptime(time_str, time_format)
        dt_utc = dt_naive.astimezone(timezone.utc)
    except ValueError:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid time format in CLF line: {time_str}")

    # 2. Parse Status
    try:
        status = int(status_str)
        if not (100 <= status <= 599):
            raise ValueError("Status code out of range")
    except ValueError:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid status code in CLF line: {status_str}")

    # 3. Parse Size
    size = 0
    if size_str is not None:
        try:
            size = int(size_str) if size_str.isdigit() else 0
        except ValueError:
            # Should not happen if regex is correct, but for safety
            pass

    # 4. Parse Latency
    latency_ms: Optional[float] = None
    if latency_str is not None and latency_str.isdigit():
        try:
            # Latency is in microseconds, convert to milliseconds
            latency_ms = int(latency_str) / 1000.0
        except ValueError:
            pass # Keep as None if conversion fails

    # Return raw fields needed by normalize
    return (dt_utc, client, method, path, status, size, latency_ms)

def parse_jsonl(line: str) -> dict:
    """Parses a JSON line into raw, validated fields for normalization."""
    try:
        data: Dict[str, Any] = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid JSON format: {e}")

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ParseError("JSON line must be a JSON object.")

    # Required fields
    required_keys = ['ts', 'client', 'method', 'path', 'status']
    for key in required_keys:
        if key not in data:
            raise ParseError(f"Missing required key: '{key}' in JSON line.")

    # Extract and validate
    try:
        ts_str = data['ts']
        # Parse ISO 8601 string, handling 'Z' for UTC
        if ts_str.endswith('Z'):
            ts_str = ts_str[:-1] + '+00:00'
        
        # Use datetime.fromisoformat if available (Python 3.7+), otherwise rely on strptime with timezone info
        if hasattr(datetime, 'fromisoformat'):
            # Attempt to parse with fromisoformat which is robust with offsets
            utc_time = datetime.fromisoformat(ts_str).astimezone(pytz.utc) if pytz.utc else datetime.fromisoformat(ts_str) # Simple handling for demonstration
        else:
            # Fallback for older Python versions (though requirement is 3.12)
            utc_time = datetime.strptime(ts_str, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z").astimezone(pytz.utc) # Requires %z support

        client = str(data['client'])
        method = str(data['method']).upper()
        path = str(data['path'])
        status = int(data['status'])
        
        # Rule: status must be 100 to 599
        if not (100 <= status <= 599):
            raise ParseError(f"Status code {status} is outside the valid range [100, 599].")
            
    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as e:
        # Catches issues with type casting or time parsing
        raise ParseError(f"Validation error in required JSON field: {e}")

    # Optional fields
    size = 0
    latency_ms = None
    
    # Size handling
    if 'bytes' in data:
        value = data['bytes']
        if isinstance(value, (str, int)):
            try:
                s = int(value) if isinstance(value, str) and value.isdigit() else int(value)
                size = max(0, s) # Must be non-negative
            except ValueError:
                # If bytes is present but invalid, size remains 0 as per rule: None and "-" mean 0
                pass
        elif value is None or value == "-":
             size = 0
    
    # Latency handling
    if 'latency_ms' in data:
        value = data['latency_ms']
        if isinstance(value, (str, float, int)):
            try:
                l = float(value)
                if l >= 0:
                    latency_ms = l
            except ValueError:
                pass # latency_ms remains None

    # Return raw fields, letting normalize handle final checks like client/method emptiness
    return {
        "time": utc_time,
        "client": client,
        "method": method,
        "path": path,
        "status": status,
        "size": size,
        "latency_ms": latency_ms
    }

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Union, Optional, Any
import re
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
import pytz

class ParseError(ValueError):
    """Custom exception raised for parsing errors."""
    pass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Record:
    """Normalized log record."""
    time: datetime
    client: str
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    size: int
    latency_ms: Optional[float]

def normalize(time: datetime, client: str, method: str, path: str, status: Union[int, str], size: Union[int, str, None], latency_ms: Optional[Union[float, int]]) -> Record:
    """Normalises raw log fields into a validated Record."""

    # 1. Time Validation and Normalization
    if not isinstance(time, datetime):
        raise ParseError(f"Time must be a datetime object, got {type(time).__name__}")
    
    # Ensure time is timezone-aware and convert to UTC
    if time.tzinfo is None or time.tzinfo.utcoffset(time) is None:
        # Assuming naive time input should be interpreted as UTC if no info is provided, 
        # though robust parsing should ensure this upstream.
        time_utc = pytz.utc.localize(time)
    else:
        time_utc = time.astimezone(pytz.utc)

    # 2. Client Validation
    if not isinstance(client, str) or not client.strip():
        raise ParseError("Client identifier must be a non-empty string.")
    client_str = client.strip()

    # 3. Method Validation
    if not isinstance(method, str) or not method.strip() or not method.isalpha():
        raise ParseError("HTTP method must be a non-empty string of ASCII letters.")
    method_str = method.upper()

    # 4. Path Normalization
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.startswith('/'):
        raise ParseError("Path must start with '/'.")

    # Remove query parameters and fragments
    path_no_query = path.split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    
    # Collapse repeated slashes
    path_normalized = re.sub(r'/+', '/', path_no_query)

    # 5. Status Validation and Conversion
    try:
        status_int = int(status)
        if not (100 <= status_int <= 599):
            raise ParseError(f"Status code {status_int} is out of the valid range [100, 599].")
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        raise ParseError(f"Status must be an integer or string representation of an integer, got {status}.")

    # 6. Size Validation and Conversion
    size_int: int
    if size is None or str(size).strip() in ('-', ''):
        size_int = 0
    else:
        try:
            size_int = int(size)
            if size_int < 0:
                raise ParseError("Size must be a non-negative integer.")
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            raise ParseError(f"Size must be an integer or string representation of one, got {size}.")

    # 7. Latency Validation and Conversion
    latency_ms_float: Optional[float] = None
    if latency_ms is not None:
        try:
            latency_ms_float = float(latency_ms)
            if latency_ms_float < 0:
                 raise ParseError("Latency must be a non-negative number.")
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            # Keep it None if it can't be parsed as a non-negative float
            pass

    return Record(
        time=time_utc,
        client=client_str,
        method=method_str,
        path=path_normalized,
        status=status_int,
        size=size_int,
        latency_ms=latency_ms_float
    )

import math
from datetime import datetime
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Record:
    time: datetime
